document:
End subsidies on MP’s food in the House of Commons, Taxpayers paid £17 million to subsidise bars and restaurants in the House of Commons between 2018-2021. 
A 3 course meal costs £10.41. 
MP’s average salary is £84,144. 
They can afford to pay full price for their own meals!, It is a national shame that children and elderly people in this country go hungry, key workers needing food banks and warm banks, yet the tax payer is spending extortionate money to subsidise food for MP’s who earn almost 50k more than the average worker.

Increase the State Pension for people with disabilities by £25 a week, The pension wealth gap is massive and many people are struggling so an extra £25 a week can help provide stability for retired disabled workers who need it most. It is important we help those who need it. Let's make a difference together., There are over 4 million disabled workers in the UK, but only 54% are saving into a private pension.
 
The average pension wealth for people with a disability who are approaching retirement age is just £47,980.
 
More disabled people are working than ever (53%), however this is still significantly lower than non-disabled people (82%).

Increase mandatory paternity leave for fathers to at least 12 weeks with pay., Increase paternity leave for fathers to at least 12 weeks. 2 weeks at full pay and 10 weeks at statutory pay. This should not detract from mother’s maternity leave and pay. This will allow better support for families., Giving birth and having a newborn is extremely difficult for mothers. They need support to recover physically, emotionally and also raising a new baby. Having fathers at home for longer than the current 2 weeks would be a great help. Mothers who have Caesarean sections are bedbound for first few weeks as well and mothers need help and support. Post natal support is very lacking for new mothers. Shared parental leave does not allow for both parents to be off at the same time.

Do not deduct Carer's Allowance from Universal Credit, With beds filling up hospitals and being blocked due to social care being underfunded and full to capacity, the Government should do more to support unpaid carer's, by ending deductions from Universal Credit for Carer's Allowance. Taking in a family member to support and care for could free up beds., Unpaid carers often need to reduce the amount they work to provide care, but then have their Carer's Allowance taken off their Universal Credit claim, making them worse off.
 
Ending deductions of the £69.70pw Carer's Allowance could help ensure the heating can be on, ensure good nutritional food can be served, transport and parking can be paid to assist with appointments, helping to free up the NHS and social care settings.

Allow students who self-funded 1st degree to access student loan for 2nd degree, To change the eligibility for student loans so that home students who have self-funded for their 1st Bachelor, Master or Doctorate degree can still be eligible to access a student loan for their 2nd degree at the same level as the 1st., Student loans are funded by the Government, and so the taxpayer, so that students can pursue an education that will hopefully land them a job and in turn become taxpayers who pay off their loans to replenish the system.
 
We believe that the existing rules, where an applicant who has self-funded their first degree is not eligible for a student loan, is draconian since the applicant has not previously accessed a student loan.

Reduce student university fees., I would like Parliament to discuss the amount of debt students are left with after University. Due to having the debt of a student loan, a large amount of money is taken out of your salary. For the amount that your salary is reduced by, it doesn’t correspond to the amount of University time we have., As a University student, I am in University 5 months out of the 12. This is the case for everyone around me who goes to University. Additionally, the amount of time that is spent in University each week is a small amount, having the online lectures now as well, some people are hardly ever in. This works fine if they believe that’s the amount of time needed for each course but it shouldn’t be at the price we are having to pay, considering the amount of time we are there.

Issue grants to repay Covid Bounce Back Loans up to £8,000 for small businesses, Provide grants so small businesses can pay off Covid Bounce Back Loans of up to £8,000. Give small businesses a chance in the cost of living crisis to keep providing for their families and keep their businesses going that they worked hard for., A lot of businesses weren’t entitled to grants so had to resort to Bounce Back Loans when they were most vulnerable. Businesses could borrow up to £50,000 depending on how big their business was. Issuing grants to enable businesses to replay off loans of up to £8,000 would help so many small businesses out by not having that burden over their shoulders for the next 6 years, especially in the cost of living crisis. Give small businesses a chance to succeed in one of the hardest times ever.
 
Any tax increases to fund these grants should only apply to businesses that benefited from these loans, and should be set at a rate that spreads the financial burden over a longer period than the repayment terms for these loans.

Petitions gaining more than 500,000 signatures should force a referendum, Legislation should be enacted to force a referendum if a parliamentary e-petition gains more than 500,000 signatures., The current e-petition system can be ignored by an incumbent government.
 
True democracy requires the incumbent government to listen to the people and e-petitions are supposed to be a way to do this, but they are too often ignored.
 
Forcing a referendum for very popular e-petitions would be a way to ensure that the Government cannot ignore e-petitions.

Exempt people on Attendance Allowance from vehicle tax, Disabled people are exempt from vehicle tax if they receive Disability Living Allowance or Personal Independence Payment, but not if they receive Attendance Allowance (for those over retirement age). Treat all disabled people equally, and exempt people on Attendance Allowance from vehicle tax., The system needs to be fairer and not ageist. The Government discriminating against the elderly. The vast majority of affordable adapted mobility cars are in a higher tax bracket, this is due to the size of vehicle and subsequent engine size. Many elderly disabled people simply don't have the choice to have a smaller care. I want to Government to ensure that people on Attendance Allowance are exempted from vehicle tax, the same as it is for those who receive other disability benefits.

Write off student loans for NHS workers after 10 years of service, We want the Government to write off student loan debt for NHS workers after 10 years of service. This is to incentivise more workers to remain employed by the NHS, as well as to help mitigate the below inflation pay rises we have seen over so many years., After 10 years of service doctors and nurses and other NHS staff will have paid back thousands of pounds of student loans, but most will still have significant student loan debts. The low take home pay for many NHS workers is driving highly skilled workers out of the work force, or overseas towards higher salaries. Rewarding loyalty to the NHS could help staff will feel valued, improve morale, and reduce gaps in staffing. This could ultimately help improve the quantity of care for our patients.

Allow children to receive DLA up to the age of 18 years old, Current rules mean that children can only receive Disability Living Allowance (DLA) up to the age of 16, and then must apply for Personal Independence Payment (PIP). We believe children should be able to receive DLA until the age of 18.,

Make Valentine day a bank holiday, The UK has the lowest number of bank holidays in the western world with the EU averaging 12 days we only get 8 in a year., Making St Valentine's day a bank holiday will give people the opportunity to spend time with their loved ones, and take holidays.
 
We believe an extra bank holiday would also help improve the wellbeing of workers, by giving many a break between the last bank holiday in January and the Easter break.

Stop the exploitative practice of unpaid internships for students., Make it mandatory for all employers in the UK to pay a minimum wage to their student interns., Brands are exploiting the fact that we are students to use us for free labour. 

The companies we work for often would not be able to produce the work they do without us or without hiring employees to replace us. 

A lot of us have to resort to working, sometimes 30+ hours, in addition to working as interns just to be able to survive. 

Companies should be required to pay a salary for any work that is done for them and the fact that we are student interns should not change that fact.

Reform e-petitions - votes at 500k, no word limits, immediate publication, Implement a new parliamentary petitions process that:
 - requires a vote in the House of Commons on the request of petitions with over 500k signatures
- removes limits on the length of petitions
- publishes petitions immediately.
, Only petitions containing offensive content should be removed.
 
We believe the current petitions process is flawed because it does not result in MPs voting on the request of a petition. Debates are usually held once 100k signatures are reached but these rarely result in change.
 
Character limits in the current process can make it difficult to articulate what action you want the Government to take. I believe the majority of mine have been rejected on these grounds.
.

Remove 6 year limit on paying voluntary NI Contributions to repair gap in record, Allow people with gaps in their National Insurance record to make voluntary contributions to repair gaps from more than 6 years ago., It's common to get a State Pension forecast when approaching retirement. Sometimes this will show gaps in your NI record caused by missing a few weeks when changing job many years ago. Anything less than the full 52 weeks of NI contributions results in THAT WHOLE YEAR NOT BEING COUNTED, so if it took 2 weeks to switch jobs you pay 50 weeks but get NOTHING for that year, if you didn't get National Insurance credits. Currently it is only possible to pay voluntary contributions to repair gaps occurring within the last 6 years. We believe that's unfair, and this limit should be removed.

Create an Adoption Allowance for self-employed adopters, Treat self-employed people equally by creating an Adoption Allowance for self-employed adopters, that provides support equal to Statutory Adoption Pay.
, Myself and my husband are unable to have children of our own, and after a long battle of trying to conceive, and many difficult conversations, we decided to adopt.

We overcame many challenges and hurdles to get this far, but because we are both self-employed we do not receive any financial support. My husband didn't take any time off and I went back to work after 5 months.
 
I believe children who are adopted by self-employed people deserve the same rights as any other child to build attachments with their parents, and introducing an Adoption Allowance for self-employed adopters would help support this.

Require first aid kits and fire extinguishers in all HGV vehicles, To meet their health and safety obligations, most employers provide first aid kits and fire extinguishers in work places. We are asking for a specific health and safety regulation requiring first aid kits and fire extinguishers in all HGV vehicles, to help ensure the safety of lone HGV drivers., We are asking that the Government recognise the specific health and safety risks to lone HGV drivers, and make it a legal requirement for there to be first aid kits and fire extinguishers in all HGV vehicles.
 
At present there is a huge variation in the provision and maintenance of first aid kits and fire extinguishers. The stark reality is that too many employers do not provide these basic safety tools.

Allow disabled people to keep all their benefits if they move in with a partner, Under current rules, people on ESA or UC risk losing some or all of our benefits if we find love and move in with a partner. This means that we have to choose either happiness or financial independence. These unfair rules have discouraged me from looking for love at any point in my life., Disabled people on income-related benefits risk being left totally dependent on their partner if they move in together. This is because, when joint income is taken into account, their partner's earnings or savings often exceed the limits for eligibility for income-related benefits

This rule applies even if the disabled person in the relationship cannot and won't ever be able to work, meaning that they have no choice other than to hope their partner's income is enough for them both to live on.

Remove need for consent from married spouse to legally change surname, If a woman in an acrimonious divorce that is taking time to finalise wants to change her surname back to her maiden name she can only do this by deed poll. To enrol this with the courts she must provide written consent from her spouse to the deed poll forms., A divorced woman will have a final order from the court stating her marriage has ended. Many organisations will accept these as proof of a name change.
 
A woman who is still married can only change her surname by deed poll and to enrol this with the courts must attach a permission letter from her spouse stating they have no objection. This can allow a spouse to control an ex-partner, and disproportionately affects women.

Allow people to pay their mortgage through salary sacrifice, The Government should allow all mortgage contributions towards an individual's main residence / family home to be made through salary sacrifice, prior to tax and national insurance deductions (similar to pension contributions)., This would allow more people to become mortgage free sooner in life and put more towards their and their children's future. It could also help divorced couples, where people are having to start life all over again, on their own, at a late age. The rising cost of living and house prices makes paying off a mortgage extremely challenging for many people.
 
The value of the mortgage that people could pay off using salary sacrifice could be capped, so that it only benefited those who are in need.

Increase financial support for 4th/5th year medical students on NHS bursaries, Medical students in their 4th and 5th year should be entitled to financial support that adequately covers their cost of living. The NHS bursary scheme should be increased in these years. Additionally, these students should have access to a full SFE maintenance loan, not a reduced rate., Years 4 and 5 of medical school can be the most challenging. Students are often on placement 5 days a week whilst studying for written and clinical examinations. Our Government should be ensuring that financial support for these students adequately covers the cost of living. We believe it currently does not. As a result, many students are facing additional pressure on top of placement and studies. In some cases, the NHS bursary and reduced-rate maintenance loan do not even cover rent payments. They deserve better.

Increase the High Income Child Benefit Charge threshold in line with inflation , The Government should increase the High Income Child Benefit Charge threshold in line with inflation since this was set in 2013. , In 2013 the High Income Child Benefit Charge was introduced, with the target of recuperating child benefit paid to families where one or more parents were classed as 'high earners'. 
 
At this time, £50,000 was deemed as the lower threshold for a high earner. In 2023, this limit remains unchanged despite inflation. 
 
As a result the current HICBC penalises working families who no longer fall within the 'high earner' category.

Stop the avoidance of child maintenance payments by working cash in hand, Parents should not be allowed to get away with not paying child maintenance because they work cash in hand, or claim to have a zero income. Many of these parents fraudulently claim benefits, then the receiving parent is told other debts take priority over child maintenance., The child maintenance service are facilitating financial abuse. Paying child maintenance should not be something you can opt out of.

Reform the High Income Child Benefit Charge for families, Change the High Income Child Benefit Charge so it only applies to households with total earnings of over £100k, or where one parent earns over £80k., We believe it is unfair that households where one parent earns £60k cannot benefit from child benefit but a household where both parents earn £30k receive the full benefit child benefit.

Father Alienation and secret court and non-molestation order should be stopped, Fathers should have the same rights in court as a mothers. One million men, 10.3% of all fathers and 5% of all men, don't live with their children. 33% can't see their children for no good reason, Change the family court to a open court so it's a fair judgment ( secret family court should be stopped. Because they don't listen to fathers if they represent themselves, or taken seriously with evidence, witness or perjury. If a parent has never sexually abused or physically abused  their child they should still have rights to see them.

Help with childcare costs for Universal Credit claimants for all unpaid carers, Currently Universal Credit claimants must be in work in order to be able to claim  back up to 85% of childcare costs. This means that anyone who is a full-time unpaid carer, but is not also in paid work, is not entitled to help with childcare costs. This is true for single or joint claims., We want help with childcare to be extended to all unpaid carers claiming Universal Credit, because the carer, while unpaid, is working at least full time as a carer. And yet, they do not get the same support with childcare as claimants in paid employment. This is particularly unfair where someone is an unpaid carer for a partner who cannot work.
 
This means unpaid carers are responsible for their children as well as their caring responsibilities, and we believe should be entitled to the same help with childcare as someone in paid work. A person in paid work is likely to have a higher income than an unpaid carer, and the costs of even part-time childcare can be totally unaffordable to parents who are unpaid carers.

Split the fees for CMS child maintenance equally between parents, Change the fees for child maintenance payments made through the Child Maintenance Service by Collect and Pay so these are divided equally between the paying parent and receiving parent., We believe it is outrageous that the paying parent has to pay a 20% fee on top of their child maintenance payment, but the receiving parent only has a 4% fee taken off the amount they receive. These fees should be divided equally between to two parties.

To stop deducting carers allowance from benefits, To stop deducting carers from our benefits 
Us carers who struggle to look after our families etc get penalised and have it removed off of benefits. We on carers save the government millions every year for caring for families and close relatives. For a low amount then get the whole lot deducted, To stop deducting carers from benefits and penalising us for saving your government millions which leaves us out of pocket.

Make a £2000 one of payment for people on Carers Allowance., Carers are financially marginalized and overshadowed in England, looking after their loved one's. Carers deserve a one off payment of £2000, Carers include stay at home Mums, Dads, Sisters, Nans, and Friends who have stopped their career to provide carer's support. 

They are the National Heroes. People on Carer's Allowance need a one off payment of £2000.

Keep the Couples Administrative Earnings Threshold (AET) for Universal Credit, It was announced in the Spring 2023 Budget that the couples Administrative Earnings Threshold (AET) is set to be scrapped, meaning non-working or low earning members of a couple can be required to comply with work search or take up offers of work, or face sanctions., This is a very broad approach that does not take into account individual family circumstances.
 
For example, in our family in order for me to be able to work (we have children but no access to suitable childcare, even with the governments new proposals which do not come into affect properly for many years) it would mean my husband having to drastically reduce his availability/hours at work in a high paid job to enable me to work for NMW.
 
We would be worse off and actually have to rely on Universal Credit MORE to bridge the gap in loss of earnings. The couples AET needs to remain.

Apply tax and NI to household income for families with children under 11, Make income tax and National Insurance apply at a household level (with tax allowances and tax band thresholds at twice the rate as for individuals) for families with children under 11., Single parents of children under 11 should also benefit from the same household tax rates.
 
Example:
 
Family 1: only one person works and earns £120,000
 
Family 2: two people earn £60,000
 
Family 1 receives approximately £13,000 less after all tax and NI is taken.
 
Although there is free childcare available, many families don’t want to use childcare in early years and shouldn’t be penalised for doing so.
 
The US and other countries apply a similar concept.

Require sanitary products be provided in all public restrooms, It’s a battle for women as it is to change sanitary products, but to not even provide them in a public restroom, even at a cost, is unacceptable. On behalf of all females I would like sanitary products to be required to be provided in all public restrooms, at a cost or not., Recently I was in the cinema and my period started, I had no sanitary products on me and when speaking to the manager he provided no help or no reason to why sanitary product are not provided.
 
Many public restrooms provide machines charging £1 for sanitary product but this restroom didn’t even have that. I was in a place where I could do nothing and had to leave the facility and go to a separate shop to buy a whole box just to use one tampon in that moment. That’s not right and needs to be changed.

Credit all carers with national insurance contributions historically, At the moment carers are only eligible for home responsibilities protection from 1978 if the person for whom they were caring  was receiving certain benefits. There is no credit for those who cared for disabled people who received severe disablement allowance, HNCIP or a retirement pension., The current situation is unfair and illogical. All carers should receive national insurance credits for the years where they cared for someone so that they are not penalised for giving up work in those circumstances.

Increase the married tax allowance where only one household member is working, Increase married tax allowance where only one household member is working.
Where both parties work and earn £25,000 a year each or £50,000 combined, they will pay £2,486 each or £4,972 combined.
Where only one member of the household earns the same £50,000, with married tax allowance, pay £7,234., This means that a household where two people are working compared to a household where only one is working would be £2,262 better off per year because of income tax and how the married tax allowance is worked out.

Households where only one member is working are being penalised just because they have a single earner.
 
Single earner households are also less likely to be entitled to other benefits.

Do not raise the UC Administrative Earnings Threshold for single parents, Do not raise the earnings threshold (AET) single parent Universal Credit claimants need to meet - in order not have to meet a Work Coach - to 18 hours a week at the national minimum wage. We believe this change is unfair on single parents, who may not be able to work more hours., I work in a nursery. I cannot do any more hours than that because they do not have the hours for me. Like many single parents, I do not have anyone who can look after my child. Please stop treating single parent households the same as two parent households. Please don't do this to single parents.

Allow people who came to the UK as international students to apply for ILR, People who came to the UK as international students have spent tens of thousands of pounds on tuition fees, visas and associated charges. Given this, we believe this group should be able to apply for Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR) after five years, rather than 10.,

Provide full-time parent carers of disabled children with £332.50 a week, Some parents are unable to work as they need to provide full-time care to their child, through the day or the night or for both. We want the Government to introduce a benefit for parents who are full-time carers of their disabled children, set at £332.50 a week (35 x minimum wage of £9.50 an hour)., There is not enough support to help with the loss of income for parents that are unable to work and need to provide full-time care to their disabled children. The child’s DLA does not replace an income, it is to ‘help with extra costs of looking after a child’ with disabilities. The Carer's Allowance benefit equates to £1.99 an hour for 35 hours a week, and is ‘a benefit that provides some financial recognition that a carer may not be able to work full-time’. Many parents who are full-time carers to disabled children will not be eligible for Universal Credit.

Many nurseries and schools are not trained or equipped to cater for all disabilities, and the Government should support all parents who need to be full-time carers for their disabled children.

Stop CMS sharing paying parents financial details with receiving parents, We want the Government to stop the Child Maintenance Service (CMS) from sharing financial information (pay, pension contributions) of paying parents with receiving parents. Receiving parents should be given the amount of maintenance they will receive, not the financial details of the paying parent., I am in a salaried position and object to my income and pension contributions being shared to someone who I have do not have an amicable relationship with. This information is private to me and I do not wish for it to be shared with people who may then choose to disclose it more widely, for example on social media.

Remove additional work restrictions for those on visas, The cost of living crisis is upon us: inflation continues and the Bank of England has recently increased base rate to 4.25%. The effects of these for food and rental costs are obvious and everyone feels it. However, immigrants are especially disadvantaged because of restrictions on additional work., Families can help themselves in the ongoing cost of living crisis by reducing expenses and or increasing their income through additional work. Immigrant families are disproportionally affected because their visa restricts the type of additional work and/or the number of additional hours they can do. In addition, they are ineligible to seek public funds. I am therefore requesting the Government remove these restrictions to allow immigrant families to do any additional work which can help them get by in these challenging times.

Create new rights to paid breastfeeding breaks for mothers, The law doesn’t require employers allow employees time off for breastfeeding. We want this to change, so that mothers have a right to paid breaks for breastfeeding. Currently some employers either don't allow, or pay for, breaks for breastfeeding mothers., Breastfeeding has benefits for a child's health and development, and supporting breastfeeding at work can help encourage mothers to go back to work and breastfeed for longer, and avoid health risks when returning to work for breastfeeding mothers. It could also help reduce staff absence, increase morale and loyalty, and help with staff retention.

Create a medal for people who gave service during the Covid-19 pandemic, To create a medal to award to persons who have provided service during the Covid-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom (including posthumously to those who have since died) but have not already received and do not qualify for other awards, to be called "The Civil General Service Medal (C.G.S.M.).", The proposed C.G.S.M. should be automatically awarded (unless refused by the recipient):

- Persons registered with their local Social Services Department at the time as a Carer for a Qualifying Person and Recipients of Carers' Allowance/Carers' Premium (as they helped keep the NHS from becoming overwhelmed)
- Carers and other essential workers
- Staff and volunteers at foodbanks (especially those that supplied vulnerable people during the pandemic)
- Emergency and NHS staff

Make NHS Dentistry treatment a priority for all., Our NHS dentist has gone to the private sector, we are unable to get treatment until our practice finds another. We are still on their list but how likely is it we will get another NHS dentist?, The reasons I have seen for the chaos in NHS dentistry seem to be all pay related. I am on a local forum, their are many stories similar to mine:
*Cancelled appointments. 
*Poor treatment.
*Inability to find an open NHS list.
*Being told your NHS registered dentist has left the practise to work privately. 

Most issues I have seen, seem to stem from the massive gap between their earnings in the private sector and what they receive as an NHS dentist. 
People health is being negatively impacted!

Make foreign students living in the UK for five years eligible for NHS LSF, Many foreign students are not entitled to student loans which means they are automatically not entitled to the NHS Learning Support Fund. We believe this is not fair as foreign students have the same amount of placement hours in the NHS as students who do qualify for support., Foreign students have the same subjects/placement hours required in a healthcare course. We are all required to achieve the same thing in order to get the degree. It is not fair that foreign students cannot access the NHS LSF because they are not eligible for student finance. We want foreign students who have been residing in the UK for over 5 years to be able to access the NHS LSF bursary just because they do not qualify for student loans. Please make a change and help us have a smooth journey as students.

Create an LGBTQ+ bank holiday ( Diversity day), We believe the country deserves at least another one bank holiday because we lack what other countries have. We should have a bank holiday to specifically recognise the diversity in the country and celebrate it and show that we care about all groups of people in the UK, We need to have more bank holidays and more diversity and to celebrate it rather than demonise it which is what we are doing to our minority groups.

Increase the 40% tax bracket from £50,270 to £70,000, With the current cost of living crisis the general public are working all hours humanely possible to stay afloat. We want the Government to raise the 40% tax threshold from the £50,270 to £70,000, so people lose a smaller proportion of their income to tax., Just like all costs rising with inflation, I believe the tax bracket should be increased too. there is a much bigger salary range between 40% and 45% than their is between 20% and 40% just that extra lift to £70,000 would make would help people with the cost of living, or to save for their future.

Increase the income tax personal allowance to £21,000 and link to inflation, We believe it's unacceptable for low paid workers and pensioners to pay tax on anything below £21,000, which is just over what someone would earn working 38 hours a week at the National Living Wage. The revenue should be recovered from those in higher earner brackets (over £140,000) and businesses., We believe the current system is unfair to those on low wages and pensions. No one earning or receiving other income of under £21,000 a year should pay income tax, and this should be increased in line with inflation in future. Many people are in crisis - we believe it is time that those who are better placed to pay, do so.

Make child maintenance payable up to 23 and increase maintenance payments, I am petitioning the Government to reform how child maintenance works. Specifically, I am calling for an extension of child maintenance payments until the child reaches the age of 23, and an increase in the amount of payments., Fatherless children are at higher risk of poverty, teenage pregnancies, crime, and mental health issues. Extending child maintenance until age 23 and increasing payments could help provide stability to support children's basic needs and education. The Government has a responsibility to ensure every child's success.

Increase the tax-free allowance threshold for those earning under £25k per year, I would like the Government to increase the tax-free allowance of those earning under £25k per year., By doing this, lower earners will be financially better off and this will help to decrease the burden of increasing energy and food prices both in the present and future.

Ensure all NHS bank staff in England receive non-consolidated payments, We want the Government to ensure that all NHS bank staff in England, who have worked tirelessly for the NHS under Agenda for Change but are not directly employed by NHS trusts, receive non-consolidated payments as part of the NHS pay deal., Because it is unfair that some NHS staff will receive one-off payments and others won't when they do exactly the same jobs and worked through Covid, covering all areas of healthcare with dedication and flexibility. Scotland and Wales bank staff are set to receive these payments. We believe it is unacceptable that many of their English counterparts are not.

Introduce mental health days for people effected with mental health., Allow workers to take mental health days that will not effect their attendance at work. Sometimes a single day to recuperate is needed in order to boost someone's mental health., "More than 15 million people - 30% of the UK population - live with one or more long-term conditions, and more than 4 million of these people will also have mental health problems."  -  Mental health foundation 

We need help the millions of people who suffering with long term mental health conditions, As a teacher mental health is something many teachers suffer and we as a collective need to allow people to actually care for their selves.

Reform maternity, paternity, shared parental & adoption leave and pay, Introduce a single entitlement to one year of leave per family. This would be shared as preferred by the parents, with an equal split as the default.
All leave should be paid at usual salary, partly funded by the government, and partly by the employer (with larger employers contributing more).
, The gender pay gap is mostly driven by women reducing time at work to care for children. Many young couples want to share work and childcare more equally but find it financially difficult with the current government policy. Reform can support more gender equal parenting, enabling more active fatherhood and empowering women at work.
Additionally, birth rates are at a historic low. Urgent action is needed so young people can afford to have kids, including well-paid parental leave.

Legal requirement for employers to provide sanitary products, There are no legal requirements for employers to provide sanitary products. Government needs to change it's health and safety legislation to ensure that women have access to products when required., Other petitions have requested free products, or time away from work. This petition is asking the Government to ensure that all companies who provide toilets and employ women to provide access to sanitary products in the workplace.

Give NHS Bank staff what they deserve! Fair pay deal too!, I want them to realise that 30% of the work force and daily shifts are picked up by bank staff with hospitals. This means bank staff who are employed directly from the nhs trusts, under the same agenda for change pay scheme. But have been left out of any pay deal!, During covid nearly 40% of the nhs work force had to work from home or  shield. (Yet didn’t work but are still getting the deal!) Meaning more gaps, unsafe staffing during a global pandemic, potential of ward closures if  bank staff did not step up and help and cover those gaps. 
Bank staff although are 0 hours are there to help trusts when they are at critical low staffing levels going above and beyond to fill gaps even last minute when staff phone in sick at short notice! Yet are excluded!

Increase number of bank holidays in England and Wales, Increase bank holidays from 2024 onwards from 8 to10 days minimum., We in England & Wales have less bank holidays than any other European country, and less than the devolved nations! I believe it would benefit the working population to increase.

Reduce higher rate income tax from 40% to 30% for income under £150k, Review the % of income tax for those earning £150,000 or less to help put money back into the economy., There is too much of a jump from 20% to 40% for those earning £150,000 or less. Reduce that jump to 30% for those who qualify for 40% income tax. Perhaps keep the threshold at 40% for those who have a basic salary of over £150,000.
 
Up to £40,000 = 20%
£40,001 - £150,000 = 30%
£150,001 - £250,000 = 40%
£250,000 + = 45%

Require all banks to provide a specific reason for closing a bank account., We request that the government asks all bank account providers to amend their terms and conditions to include a mandatory clause that requires all banks to provide a specific written report (not generic wording) detailing why a bank account was closed upon written request from the customer., In an age of ever increasing censorship many independent content creators are being removed from banking services without any warning or reason. These methods of account closure can be subject to internal abuse, staff members with particular ideologies or prejudices may have the ability to close the account of businesses and individuals that they do not like without any reason. This is an unacceptable way to treat a client and the disruption in their day to day business can be catastrophic.

Extend deadline and provide funding for supported housing to achieve EPC rating, We ask the Government to increase the time frame and provide funding for sheltered and supported housing groups so that they have a better chance of achieving the Government’s housing energy standards., Some supported housing groups are at risk of closure. Elderly and vulnerable residents are frightened, and want to stay in the supported environment that the homes create for them.

The Government require that all privately rented homes and fuel poor homes achieve an EPC rating of C by 2030. We believe that for some supported housing groups this time frame is too short. In some cases, finances to carry out these upgrades have been impacted by economic circumstances and the covid pandemic. We also ask the government to provide funding for supported homes at risk of closure due to the costs of the energy efficiency upgrades.

Allow international students and those with graduate visas to bring dependents, The Home Office has announced plans to place limits on international students bringing their dependents. We believe this is unreasonable, and contrary to human rights., We believe this is not a welcoming policy for our economy and will not encourage students to choose the UK. The UK Government could lose billions of pounds because of such harsh and unwelcoming policies.
 
This country is facing a shortage of workers and this policy may mean that international students, who could contribute to the future workforce, choose to go to Australia, Canada, or New Zealand instead.
 
The Government should allow international students to bring their dependents on a student visa or when they get a graduate visa (Post-Study Work visa - PSW).

Allow households to combine personal income tax thresholds, Allow households to choose whether to opt for taxation using personal thresholds or 'family thresholds', where personal thresholds are combined, as families with one higher rate earner pay tax at a higher rate even if their overall income would be within a combined standard rate tax threshold., Families can be taxed more as a household because an individual may have a higher salary, for example:
 
Family 1 has 2 parents, 1 earning £8,000 a year and another earning £60,000. Family 2 has 2 parents, both on £35,000 a year.
 
Family 1 does not benefit from Child Benefit payments as they are deemed to earn too much, and have almost £10,000 taxed at the higher rate tax, whereas family 2 are able to fully benefit from Child Benefit and pay less in tax than family 1 but have a higher gross annual income.

Base NHS pay award on worked hours in 22/23 and not contracted hours on 31/03/23, To revisit how the non-consolidated payments for 22/23 for NHS staff are calculated. It should be calculated based on the worked hours in 22/23 (except overtime) instead of solely looking at contracted hours on 31/03/2023., We believe the current award is not fair to NHS staff who have changed their contracted hours during the 22/23 period. With the pandemic eased, some NHS staff may have changed their contracted hours focusing on other aspect of their life. We believe it is unreasonable to overlook the work that staff had put in during 22/23 and look solely at contracted hours on one day, 31/03/2023, as the pay deal was branded 22/23. This is essentially uncredited the work particular staff had contributed, please re-consider.

Fund free NHS paternity tests at birth, We believe that too many men end up raising someone else's child, and don't find out at all or for many years. We want the Government to provide funding for NHS paternity tests at birth, so fathers can find out if they are a child's biological father.,

Ensure that ALL Nurses on AFC,working for a non NHS employer receive the bonus., Treat all Nurses fairly and pay the full pay increase of 5% and the bonus top up to ALL Nirses who are on Agenda For Change, even if they work for a non NHS employer., Because all Nurses should be treated equally and fairly.  Most of us worked through the Pandemic when other services closed their doors. Even though we work for external companies, we treat NHS Patients, are on AFC, have NHS emails and pay into an NHS Pension, we are exempt form the bonus aspect of the pay deal.

Fund the consolidated NHS payment to all agenda for change community services, Give funding to all community run NHS services so that their staff can receive the consolidated payment., You are not funding the one off payment.

This will damage the morale and structure of teams in the community and lead to unsafe staffing levels which will directly affect patient care. 

We worked through covid just the same as any other service and feel completely de-valued by this decision. 

We do the same job and we are on agenda for change so why are we treated differently? Why are we entitled to the payrise, but not the one off payment? This makes no sense at all.

Recalculate child maintenance payments for income changes below 25% threshold, Child Maintenance Service (CMS) does not recalculate payments unless a parent's income changes by more than 25%. The Government should ensure that CMS accept evidence of paying and/or non-paying parents’ income changes even below a 25% income threshold, so long as evidence is provided. , Every pound matters towards a child getting its right towards income contribution from both its parents. CMS has been rejecting evidence merely on the grounds of income changes being just shy of their 25% threshold mark. The impact on payments can be significant.

Extend family visas to all parents of British citizens, Currently parents of British citizens are only eligible for family visas in specific circumstances. We want family visas to be extended to all parents of British citizens, to make it easier for British citizens to be joined in the UK by their parents.,  
We believe the current system is unfair, and it can be difficult and costly for British citizens wanting to be joined in the UK by their parents to prove that their parents are eligible for a family visa under the current system.
 
The current system restricts British citizens from being joined and supported by their family, which can have an adverse impact on their mental health. We want all parents of British citizens to be able to enter the UK on a family visa.

Recognize the efforts of all NHS bank staff and give them the lump sum payment., We are disheartened regarding the decision made by the NHS England about the lump sum payment for the year 2022/2023. Bank staff who worked as substantive staff within the NHS but resigned and continued as bank staff before March 31, 2023, are denied this well-deserved payment in England., The government's decision fail to acknowledge and appreciate the contributions of bank staff, many of whom were previously substantive staff. Denying them the non-consolidated lump sum payment feels like a betrayal of their loyalty and dedication. This raises concerns about fairness in the pay rise allocation. I respectfully urge the government to reconsider and ensure that the pay rise is fair and inclusive, recognizing the contributions of bank staff who have served as substantive staff.

Increase High Income Child Benefit Charge threshold and base on household income, We want the Government to reform the High Income Child Benefit Charge (HICBC) by increasing the income threshold for this charge to take into account inflation since 2013, and make it apply to household income, not individual income., Due to the Government’s policy of not increasing the threshold for HICBC, this charge now affects 1 in 5 families, raising over £1 billion each year for HMRC.
 
We believe the way the charge works is outdated and does not take into account  inflation since 2013 or household incomes. Inflation means that the current £50,000 threshold is no longer a high income, and basing the charge on individual, rather than household income, means some households liable for the charge have lower incomes than households that do not have to pay the charge.

Impose restrictions on benefits and allowances for former Prime Ministers, Former Prime Ministers are entitled to benefits such as the Ministerial Severance Pay and the Public Duties Cost Allowance currently set at a limit of £115,000 per year. Only those who have served a minimum 1-year term and not been sanctioned by the House of Commons should qualify for this., Following a series of short terms served by unelected (by the public) PM's during recent years, and a former Prime Minister being found to have misled the House of Commons this change needs to happen.

Allow petitions about nominations for peerages, I want the Parliament to remove the restrictions within the petitions standards on calling for the removal of nominations for peerages. We believe it serves only to protect the systemic cronyism exploited through this archaic process., We believe public standards of our elected representatives continue to fall deeper and deeper beneath what would have been rock bottom in any other era, and that the public should be allowed to petition against nominations for peerages, where they find these unacceptable.
 
There is no mechanism for democratic review of these nominations that seem increasingly to be awarded solely on the basis of political patronage.
 
In the absence of a proper reform or removal of the peerage system, a public right to reply seems appropriate.

Create legal requirements for employers to increase worker's pay each year, We believe the pay every worker in the UK earns should be increased each year. We want the Government to pass legislation to require employers to increase their workers’ pay each year, starting with 2% (the Government's target inflation rate) this year, then by inflation for every future year., Many people have seen no change to their pay while inflation has been very high. We believe there should be a legal requirement for employers to increase their workers' pay each year.

Provide ringfenced funding for local libraries, Libraries across the country are being closed, cut back and/or outsourced to volunteers as a result of government cuts to local authority budgets. Many councils are struggling to keep staffed library services open when faced with the competing demands of social care, child protection etc., Libraries offer a place for education and opportunity – our libraries are a gateway for many people to access a blue badge, a bus pass, friendships as well as a vital resource for the promotion of reading.
 
They are a important for the digitally excluded who need to go online to access benefits, health, education and employment resources.
 
The Government must ringfence funding to ensure councils can fulfil their statutory duty to keep libraries services available to the general public. The Government must ringfence funding to ensure councils can fulfil their statutory duty to keep libraries services available to the general public.

Increase Carer's Allowance to 35 hours a week at the minimum wage, We want the Government to increase the amount of Carer's Allowance to match pay for a full-time job., Being an unpaid carer is a full-time job, and this should be reflected in the rate of Carer's Allowance.
 
Unpaid carers eligible for Carer's Allowance receive £76.75 a week to provide at least 35 hours of care to people in receipt of certain benefits. This is almost £300 less than someone earning the National Living Wage (age 23 or over) would be entitled to.
 
Many unpaid carers have to give up work to provide care, and being a carer can also have a significant impact on carers wellbeing and lifestyle. Providing appropriate financial support is the least the Government can do.

Reform Universal Credit rules for people claiming Carer's Allowance., We want the Government to:

Stop taking Carer's Allowance pound for pound off people's Universal Credit claims and take 55p for every pound instead., Pay the same rate of Universal Credit to people aged 18 to 24 claiming Carer's Allowance, as paid to those 25 and over.
 
We want the Government to better recognise people who provide unpaid care. Our job is hard enough providing care. This isn't a nine to five job it's round the clock and current rules for Universal Credit - deducting Carer's Allowance in full from entitlements, and paying a reduced rate to claimants aged under 25 - can make it hard for people on Carer's Allowance to afford to survive.

Require schools to have lunch breaks at least 40 minutes long, We want the Government to require schools to have lunch breaks that are at least 40 minutes long. Academics have argued that short lunch breaks can have potential serious implications for children’s wellbeing and development., We believe it is important for the Government to make this change so that children have the best chance to pursue academic dreams. This is only possible if students have adequate opportunities to have lunch, socialise and exercise.

Require water companies offer WaterSure to DLA, PIP, AA, CA claimants, We want the Government to require water companies to offer WaterSure to claimants of Carer's Allowance, Disability Living Allowance, Personal Independence Payment and Attendance Allowance. Currently it is up to water companies whether claimants of these benefits are eligible for WaterSure support., Many disabled or chronically ill people already face huge extra living costs, as a result of their condition. The energy crisis and cost of living crisis has already financially impacted affected disabled people massively. Currently many water companies only offer WaterSure schemes if someone claims an income-based benefit. Yet, other significant benefits have been left out. Disabled people and carers, who use extra water as a result of a condition, must be offered this support.

Require the Bank of England allow public to vote on monetary policy, Provide the public with a process that allows individuals to vote on the policies made by the central bank. This could be enabled with blockchain CBDC infrastructure., The Government are public servants who are paid through the use of national taxes. It should be their upmost priority to provide the public with a degree of leverage where possible over the decisions that affect their lives and impact them most.

Allow siblings of EU citizens resident in the UK to access the Settlement Scheme, Currently it is impossible for siblings of EU citizens resident in the UK to apply to enter the UK through the EU Settlement Scheme. The scheme allows children, grandchildren or great-grandchildren, and dependent parents, grandparents or great-grandparents to access the scheme, but not siblings., I am from Poland and have lived in England for over 9 years, and believe my siblings should be able to enter the UK under this scheme.

Require banks to give a specific, contestable reason before closing an account, Please impose the following legal requirement on banks:

"Before closing a customer's account, the bank must provide the customer with:
 
1) a valid, specific reason
 
and
 
2) an independent route of appeal."
, Banks are currently able to close customers' accounts with neither of the above, a situation which is open to abuse given that such lack of transparency could conceal the reasons for closure, up to and including something as trivial as the institution's personal dislike of either the customer or their opinions, particularly if the customer is a public figure of some description.
 
The law should require transparency and a right of appeal, and I ask that it be amended as suggested to ensure this.

Make 'National Lazy Day' a public holiday, The Government should make 'National Lazy Day' – 10 August – a public holiday. Having a lazy day gives your brain a break and your body a chance to recover. And having a lazy day can bring a lot of positive impacts for your physical and mental health.,

Change the law regarding banks shutting down customers bank accounts, Recently bank accounts of prominent campaigners have been closed without reason. This should only be allowed if the bank gives a contestable reason & should only be done by a court. Not by the bank acting unilaterally. The government must act because without a bank account, you are limited.,

Give fathers/second parents a right to 6 weeks' paid leave in baby's first year, Change parental leave and pay to give employed fathers/second parents two weeks' paternity leave, plus four weeks' non-transferable parental leave, paid at 90%, to be taken in the baby's first year. Introduce a Paternity Allowance with similar benefits for other fathers/second parents., The UK’s gender pay gap is above the EU average. Longer, better-paid leave for fathers should help support greater gender equality in the labour market: countries offering fathers more than six weeks of paid leave have smaller gender pay and labour force participation gaps. More than half of UK families struggle financially when fathers take paternity leave. Taking two weeks’ leave at the statutory rate costs an average earning father more than £1,000, and around 20% of fathers are ineligible.

Stop banks closing charity account's without giving a reason, Stop banks closing charity accounts without giving a reason., I am involved with a charity whose account has been closed and no reason given. 
There is no valid reason we know of why they should do this.
We are finding it difficult to open a new account.

Do not increase visa fees and the Immigration Health Surcharge, Halt any further increases in visa fees and the Immigration Health Surcharge. Immigrants who contribute through taxes shouldn't face increased financial burdens, We believe these fees are already an extortionate burden on individuals who hold temporary visas, with no access to public funds. It is disheartening that despite our contributions, we are required to pay additional charges just to access essential healthcare services through the NHS. It is crucial to highlight that individuals with work visas diligently fulfil their tax obligations. Yet they are subjected to policies that demand extra payments for access to the NHS. The Government should not increase these even further.

Create a baby loss bereavement support scheme for self-employed parents, The Government should create a bereavement support scheme to provide financial support for self-employed parents who experience baby loss through miscarriage, stillbirth or neonatal death. Currently there is no support for self-employed parents who are faced with this horrendous loss., There is welcome Government support available for people who lose partners and a scheme for employed parents who lose a child, but nothing for self-employed people who experience baby loss. They need time to grieve without having to worry about working and paying their bills during such a tragic situation. We want to see a change in financial support for self-employed bereaved parents.

Make school day shorter at Douay Martyrs as it gets longer with shorter breaks!!, Make the school day shorter by atleast 25 mins as in the past 2 years, the school day has extended by a total of 35 minutes. In 2020-2021, year 7 students began school at 8:45am and ended at 2:45-2:50 depending on the campus. As on 2023-2024 the school day is to begin at 8:40 and end at 3:15., At douay martyrs secondary school the school day has been extended by a total of 40 mins since September 2020-2021 as of September 2023-2024. Additionally, our breaks are being shortened, however the day is being extended which will cause students to under perform academically in all areas as they will simply be too tired and over worked. As of September 2023, the school day is set to be 6 hours and 35 minutes long, with 45 mins of that time being breaks, but in 2020 the day was 6 hours long with 45 mins of that being break.

Review the child maintenance non-resident parents are required to pay by CMS, We want a full review into the amount of child maintenance non-resident parents (NRPs) are required to pay by the CMS., We believe the existing amounts NRPs are required to pay in many cases too low, and that reforms are needed to more adequately support families.
 
Currently the NRP, if claiming benefits or with an income under £100 a week, pays only £7 per week as a flat rate towards their child.
 
We want this rate, and the amount of child maintenance all NRPs are required to pay by the CMS, to be reviewed. We believe these should better reflect the average cost of bringing up a child in the UK.
 
We believe at present far too much pressure is being put on the resident parent to ‘figure it out’ financially.

Change child maintenance calculations from gross annual earnings to Net earnings, I want the Government to change the way CMS calculates child maintenance payments, so these use net, not gross pay. Gross earnings are not what the parent takes home after all mandatory deductions are made. Calculations should therefore be based on net pay, and not gross annual earnings.
 , Child maintenance is calculated on gross annual earnings which we believe is not fair, as these parents do not receive the amount of money that the calculations are being made from! They are paying tax and National Insurance on these earning which means the CMS is calculating child maintenance using an amount that isn’t actually received by the parent.

Let carers keep their allowance – don’t reduce their other benefits, Carers undertake daily responsibility for the care and protection of another person. Yet many, forced by circumstance to rely on benefits - so they can be with their cared-for-person - face deductions.
, The clapping has stopped, now please stand up for carers.
 
Disability benefits are, rightly, protected from means testing. Not to have done so, would mean that what was given with one hand, would be snatched by another.
 
Those caring for many of these people, are not afforded the same recognition. Many will still see their Carer's Allowance swallowed up by reductions in other benefits.
 
This isn’t just about money either, there is a neglectful principle at play; the demoralising dismissal of the carer role and denial of the needs of carers, separate from those they care for.

Increase personal savings allowance, Current limits are low and don't promote savings, specially for higher and additional rate tax payers. With the increased cost of living and inflation banks have increased savings rates but with the high taxation it defeats the purpose., The Goverment should be doing their best to support the population in current times. With increased cost of living, inflation, savings become key product a large number of the population is dependent on to earn some interest.

Current accounts offer almost no interest and hence money sitting in accounts loses value due to inflation. Savings products are key and hence the limits should be increased.

Require employers to pay workers for required overtime, Whilst we have a compulsory national minimum wage compulsory within the UK, we do not have any legislation to make overtime pay compulsory., Working in hospitality/retail for over 10 years, overtime is regularly required by employers and isn’t always paid as it’s not a legal requirement.
 
Many staff are required by employers to do additional work, outside contracted hours, for no extra pay. This means that the employer can avoid taking on extra staff required to do the work. It also means the effective hourly rate of the worker is reduced.
 
I believe requiring employers to pay for overtime they require workers to do will make environments such as hospitality better places to work and will encourage leaders of businesses to increase productivity and reduce workload pressures.

Provide barge ship accommodation for MPs and remove their second home allowance., Provide "perfectly decent accomodation", for sitting MPs when in Westminister to reduce the burden placed on the public purse by the second home allowance., The burden of accommodating MPs in second homes, when performing their public duties, shouldn't rest on the tax payer if perfectly decent accommodation can be provided. Therefore, in using barge ships, like the Bibby Stockholm, we the taxpayer would see significant reductions in unnecessary costs.

Do not allow non-resident parents with CMS arrears to move off enforced payments, We want the Government to reform Child Maintenance Service (CMS) arrangements so that when a non-resident payment is paying off arrears through a deduction from earnings order, this remains in place until the arrears are cleared, and the parent not allowed to change payment method after six months., Currently after 6 months of paying via an enforced method, such as a deduction from earnings order, the paying parent has the option to move to Collect and Pay, which means the paying parent is relied upon to make the payment. Should they miss payments it can take months to set up a new deduction from earnings order, meaning the resident parent can miss out on payments during that time. We want CMS to keep enforced payment in place where a non-resident parent has child maintenance arrears, until these are cleared.

Create a Government-run bank for people who can't open an account elsewhere, I would like the Government to open and run a bank for those who are unable to open any bank account with any other bank, including a 'basic' account. This will only be for everyday banking facilities., Some are struggling to open a bank account with any bank, even with a 'basic' account, we need the Government to provide a solution.
 
The Government is able to provide a solution by creating a bank of last resort.

Make local Councillors full-time paid roles, We would like to see the role of a local Councillor change from part-time to full-time and for it to be a paid position. We also ask for these full-time councillors to be fully trained and tested in financial management and for the results of these test to be made available to the public., We believe that with recent local council failures, which could pass millions of pounds of debt to council tax payers, it’s evident that some Councillors are ill prepared to make the massive financial decisions which now fall on their shoulders. We think the part time nature of the role inhibits the full time contributions that modern councils need to make in order to provide services to residents. This structure needs to change to increase accountability on local councils.

Stop the banks making us a cashless society., Stop the banks from being able to limit how much money we can take out of our accounts at any one time, stop the bank from charging us ridiculous charges to withdraw money from a cash point ie 2.75% of the amount we will withdraw., Banks aave said from the 11th of September they will be able to limit the amount of money that a person can put in and takes out of their account, they will have the right to refuse taking cash and cheques. Banks want their customers to use electronic banking only. I believe it is against our human rights for the banks to dictate how where and when a person can spend what is legal tender (cash). This could then lead to 
People being controlled by the banks and those that run the banks as to where, when and how we can spend our own money.

If England Women's football team win the World Cup, make Monday Bank Holiday, I'd like the Government to declare a bank holiday for all workers in the United Kingdom., Then we can celebrate in the achievements of England's football team.

Remove the discretion of the Child Maintenance Service (CMS) to write off debts, The Government should remove the discretion that the CMS has to write off child maintenance debts. All debts must be paid and not written off. Parents should not be able to dodge maintenance payments. It’s entirely unacceptable., Non-paying parents should not be protected like this and should be responsible for contributing to the financial side of raising their children.

Introduce a Universal Basic Income, We want the Government to introduce a Universal Basic Income set at a high enough level to secure everyone's right to a basic standard of living, and end the need for means-tested benefits., We believe this would:
 
- Help improve people's mental health
- Recognise unpaid care and voluntary work
- Enable people to pursue work in the arts
- Provide everyone with financial independence
- Remove disincentives not to take up work
- End sanctions for benefits
- Be simpler than the current benefits system
- Provide workers with a safety net

Change the High Income Child Benefit charge to a higher or a household threshold, The High Income Child Benefit charge is unfair. The charge is imposed against individual salaries of over £50k rather than against total household income - this means children who are supported by joint parental salaries of £99k do not lose out, but children who rely on a single income of £51k do., The government has made a mistake here and they should correct this as this just doesn't make sense. 
The current High Income Charge is based on individuals salary not on a household threshold. This should be a household threshold not an individual one.

Require employers to pay employees for rest breaks, A rest break is already compulsory after 6 hours of work. However, care for workers should go further and make payment for breaks compulsory for employers. If an employer wants a worker to continue working after their compulsory break, such a break should be paid by law., The need for rest is a result of hard work and should be compensated. We think it is unfair to expect a worker to continue their duty (rest being a part of that duty after 6 hours) without being paid for their rest breaks.

Stop our only bank in Todmorden from closing. Halifax bank, Consider not closing our only bank in todmorden. Todmorden is full of a generation who do not have the facility for online banking or would not like to have their financial arrangements this way, Allow us to start a further petition to try and save this facility

Sanction Poland for failing to return abducted children to the UK, There is a UK-Poland child abduction crisis. The Government must respond decisively to Poland's failure to return abducted children to the UK. This should include withdrawing UK support - financial or otherwise - if they continue to fail to meet international obligations to return abducted children., More than 200 families report child abduction from the UK every year according to official figures. Other cases go unreported. Abduction damages children's lives and can put left-behind families in an agonising state of living bereavement. Poland is a major destination for child abduction from the UK, not only due to the large Polish community, but also because the Polish authorities are failing to return abducted children to the UK.

Reform intestacy rules when a spouse dies following a conditional divorce order, We want the Government to remove the automatic rights of a person to inherit when their spouse dies after a conditional divorce order has been granted, and the right of the spouse to become the administrator for the deceased, and so determine funeral and burial arrangements., At present a spouse inherits most or all of the deceased's estate automatically if there is no will, even if a divorce is nearing completion. They are also entitled to become the administrator of the estate, and so have total control over funeral and burial arrangements. We believe this is not fair.
 
Spouses should not automatically inherit under intestacy rules when a conditional divorce order has been granted. In these circumstances the spouse should only have the same rights as a divorcee. They should also not be entitled to become the administrator of the estate, and so have the power to decide on funeral and burial arrangements.

Require public referendums to approve Government/Parliament renovation projects, UK citizens need a greater say in how and where our money is being spent, by having any Government or Parliament proposed renovation projects, using UK tax payers money, approved by the UK public in form of a referendum., The Government release an annual statement on UK spending, but taxpayers have no real say in how or where their tax money should be spent. We have to trust our elected representatives and officials to be the caretakers and decision makers in large financial & economical decisions, but with renovations such as Big Ben, costing around £80 million, refurbishment of the Department for Education costing a reported £34 million, we believe we can no longer rely on them to fulfil their roles ungoverned.

Give one-person households 50% council tax discount rather than 25%, We believe people living on their own are unfairly burdened by the high cost of council tax, as they only receive a 25% discount., With the cost of living rising, the council tax bill can be a significant cost for households with only a single income.

Create a Minister of State for Hospitality that attends Cabinet, To create a standalone position of Minister of State for Hospitality that attends cabinet. They should be given responsibility for creating regional and national hospitality plans for the ever growing and expanding Hospitality Industry., The UK Hospitality industry represents approximately 5% of the UK GDP, 10% of employment and 6% of businesses here in the UK. As we have seen a massive decline in employment in hospitality, businesses have shut down due to staffing problems and a lack of adequate Government support. We believe the UK needs a Minister of Hospitality to meet with Hospitality representatives across the UK, and develop hospitality regional plans and plans to get more employment into the hospitality sector.

Fund free travel for 16-19 year olds that are in further education, Support all school leavers that go into further education by funding free transport. Use it as an incentive and a reward., Free travel should be available to all 16-19 year olds in further education. This supports the families to enable the child to enter further education and may make a positive contribution to later employment figures. 
 
The expense of public transport can be a barrier to young people trying to access further education. Free travel would prevent this and help more young people to pursue further education and training.
Give pensioners an allowance to get a mobility vehicle, Give pensioners the higher rate mobility allowance so that they can get a Motability car or vehicle., Equal Mobility Rights for All Seniors

Scrap student loans for tuition fees for nursing students from 2017 until 2020, Get rid of the debt that student nurses incurred for tuition fees between the years 2017-2020.

Studying nursing was free to the individual previously, then in 2017 the Government ended its system of bursaries and we had to start paying £9,250 per year., From 2020 nursing students receive a bursary and the NHS pays their tuition fees, meaning that many of those who started in 2017 have a student loan of £27,750, while most of those in earlier and later cohorts do not. We pay a lot of money to our student loan every month and many others pay nothing. It is a massive effect on our pay and it is only fair to get rid of the student loan debt for everyone.

Remove UK spouse visa financial requirement and fees for long term marriages, The Government should remove the current financial requirements and fees for spouses of British nationals where they have been married for over 6 years and are able to meet strict evidence requirements that they are in a durable relationship with their British partner. , You don't want anyone gaming the system, but after several years of marriage/ solid evidence of a durable relationship it should be fine.
 
I am in the absurd situation where I am British, my children are British, but my wife has to pay £1538 just for the first spouse visa, and from £1560 - £2350 for the NHS surcharge. I also have to prove I earn over the £18600 threshold, which means I'll need to return to the UK without my wife until I have evidence that I've earned over this threshold for six months. 

I understand the above rules for newlyweds but not serious married couples where there is clear evidence of a durable and genuine marriage

Allow partners to receive Bereavement Support when not on benefits or pregnant., The Bereavement Support Payment should be changed to ensure that regardless of whether or not you claim child benefit or are pregnant, you should still be eligible for help from the government, if you are living together as though you were married., The current criteria to be eligible is, you were married or in a registered civil partnership, or living together as though you were married. This should be it, however, if you are just living together, there is more criteria, you have to be: getting child benefit, eligible for child benefit, or pregnant. 

In times of grief, people should not have to sell their family car or take loans out to be able to pay for the funeral, or to live semi-normal life’s after such heartbreaking circumstances.

Change the way the CMS operate, I want a review into how the CMS operate. They should work out the payments based on Net pay as opposed to Gross pay. 
Household incomes on both sides need to be considered.
Placing non resident parents in fictitious arrears needs to be made illegal, Thousands of separated parents (mainly fathers) are being pushed to financial ruin from the CMS and in the worst cases, suicide.
The current CMS operating procedures are having a severe impact on the paying parents mental health as well as plunging them into debt. Enforcing fictitious arrears on parents and charging interest on those payments with little or no hope of ever getting out of them. The CMS shouldn’t be allowed to profit off of the earnings of paying parents.
